repo: gsd-tools query commit helper has a known false-negative: it can report 'commit_failed' even though the commit lands cleanly in git log — always verify with git log/git status rather than trusting the reported status.

worktree.baseRef config controls whether executor worktrees fork from 'head' (includes uncommitted-to-origin planning commits like new PLAN.md files) vs 'fresh'/origin default — must be verified before dispatching worktree executors or they can silently miss recent HEAD commits.

In this pnpm monorepo, worktree-based parallel execution requires a fresh `pnpm install` per worktree (expensive), so for waves with mostly single plans, sequential execution on the main tree is preferred over parallel worktrees despite worktrees being enabled in config.
Web-side executors must rebuild the SDK dist before running web typecheck, otherwise typecheck runs against stale SDK build artifacts (cross-package staleness landmine).

GSD plan/plan-checker executors have repeatedly mis-marked SDK-READ-0x requirements as `[x]` complete in REQUIREMENTS.md before their full acceptance criteria (including later-wave service deletions) were actually satisfied — orchestrator must audit and revert premature completion marks.

Deletion-blocking importer surfaces can be much larger than what individual plans explicitly own — e.g., Plan 11's target modules (kind-cache, file-metadata.service, etc.) had ~15+ importers across apps/web/src, several unowned by any plan (utils/fileTypes.ts, lib/crypto/key-wrapping.ts, vault-settings.store.ts, TextEditorDialog.tsx, useStreamingPreview.ts) and had to be mapped explicitly before the deletion plan could proceed.
The gap-analysis.plan-post check's JSON output can contain control characters that break naive parsing of the 'rendered' field — running the check directly (not through the wrapper) is a workaround.

code.finding: ROT-07 anti-rollback gate (RotationHighWater.enforceResolved) added at the root resolve site in resolvePublishedNode.
ROT-07 gate also added at dfsFindFolder's child-loop site, closing the read-path zero-gating gap identified in RESEARCH Pitfall 2.
Pre-existing write-path ROT-07 gate that the two new read-path gates were added alongside.

resolveChildren docstring documents the security reasoning for skip-on-failure per-child degradation: the parent folder is already gated via ensureFolderLoaded/dfsFindFolder before this runs, so an unverifiable sibling is simply omitted rather than rendered with stale/attacker content, and navigating into any child re-triggers the gate.

workflow: When a subagent reports a 'deviation' on security-adjacent code (e.g., widened error-handling on a read path), independently re-run the security-relevant tests and read the actual implementation rather than accepting the executor's self-assessment.

For pause/resume across a quota reset, compute the wake delay from a freshly-fetched current timestamp, not a timestamp captured earlier in the conversation — a stale timestamp caused a scheduled wakeup to be ~25 minutes late.
A ScheduleWakeup call cannot always be cleanly retracted; treat a stray duplicate wake as a safe no-op if the session already resumed manually, rather than trying to cancel it.

git fetch can fail in a sandboxed session with no network access; falling back to the last-known local origin/main ref is acceptable if it can be corroborated as current (e.g., it matches the fork-base of a branch created earlier that same day).
